findings.detail: Performance 1 sets the aim of achieving Established Mayoral Strategic Authority status with an Integrated Settlement. The associated activity is to maintain Integrated Settlement Readiness and support its implementation.
findings.matters: An Integrated Settlement would change how central government funding reaches the authority, which affects the funding base that finance directors and lenders rely on.
findings.quote: Ensure the authority achieves Established Mayoral Strategic Authority status, with an Integrated Settlement, as soon as possible.

findings.headline: The Combined Authority plans fire governance transition readiness activities, including financial planning, for any transfer of Fire Authority functions to it.

findings.matters: A transfer of fire functions to a combined authority would move a major service and its budget, so finance officers at constituent councils and lenders would need to track how its finances are planned.
findings.quote: Deliver Fire Governance Transition Readiness activities, including governance design, risk management, financial planning and stakeholder engagement, in preparation for any transfer of Fire Authority functions to CPCA arising from devolution legislation.

findings.matters: A finance director, here or at a peer council, can compare the stated tolerance for investment risk against their own, and a lender can see how the Authority describes its risk limits for investment activity.

findings.headline: Recommendations B to F on the Capital Transport Programme were not carried at the Transport Committee on 4 November 2026, because the required support from both constituent highways authority representatives was not secured.
findings.detail: The committee resolved to note the independent prioritisation framework and assessment of schemes, but the recommendations failed on the constitutional voting requirement. The paper states that a majority of votes were cast in favour. Recommendations B to F are repeated in this paper for the Combined Authority Board.
findings.matters: A capital programme and grant allocation can stall on a voting threshold that requires both highways authorities to agree, even when a majority of members support it.
findings.quote: despite a majority of votes being cast in favour, the recommendations were not carried.

findings.matters: A large, rising highways line is a recurring commitment that a finance director would compare with the council's other capital demands and with peer councils' highways budgets.
findings.quote: 38,768 Highways Maintenance and Pothole funding 45,026 48,701 55,676 55,676

findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare this profile with their own multi-year capital plan to see how a large programme is phased and when its peak falls.

findings.paper_title: Draft Budget 202728 and Medium-Term Financial Plan 2027-2031 and Annual Business Plan Outline 202728
findings.headline: Discretionary revenue resources fall from £16.5m in 2027/28 to £13.7m in 2030/31 as treasury income declines
findings.detail: The paper says the decline comes from lower treasury income as forecast cash balances reduce, together with the fixed nature of the other sources. Income from treasury loans is forecast to decline across the medium-term plan.
findings.matters: A finance director can see a falling base of discretionary funding over the plan, which reduces room for new spending or pressures.
findings.figures: £16.5m discretionary revenue resources in 2027/28; £13.7m in 2030/31
findings.quote: the known discretionary revenue resources available to the Combined Authority are reducing from £16.5m in 27/28 to £13.7m in 2030/31.

findings.paper_title: Draft Budget 202728 and Medium-Term Financial Plan 2027-2031 and Annual Business Plan Outline 202728
findings.headline: Business rates retention has a worst-case funding drop of c£1m in 2028/29 if the safety net falls to 92.5%, with a £3m smoothing reserve set aside
findings.detail: The paper says the 100% safety net is guaranteed for 2027/28 only. If the safety net fell to the level for local authorities in 2028/29, a fall in rates would produce a worst-case funding drop of about £1m against current grant levels. A £3m business rates smoothing and risk reserve is set aside to provide a buffer.
findings.matters: A lender or finance director can see the downside risk from a move into business rates retention and the reserve set against it.
findings.figures: c£1m worst-case funding drop; 100% safety net for 2027/28; 92.5% local authority safety net level; £3m business rates smoothing/risk reserve; 20% share of growth
findings.quote: then a worst-case position would correspond to a potential drop in funding of c£1m compared to current grant levels.

findings.paper_title: Draft Budget 202728 and Medium-Term Financial Plan 2027-2031 and Annual Business Plan Outline 202728
findings.headline: £12m a year of grant currently designated as capital is replaced by retained business rates, which are revenue
findings.detail: The paper says the replacement is pound-for-pound for 2027/28, but the retained rates are revenue income. The government has indicated that it expects capital plans to be maintained and may attach conditions. The draft budget assumes £12m a year is set aside to fund the capital programme directly.
findings.matters: A finance director at any council receiving capital grants may face the same issue: when a capital grant is replaced by a revenue income stream, the capital programme depends on how that stream is treated.
findings.figures: £12m per year of capital grant replaced; 20% share of business rates growth for the authority; 100% safety net in 2027/28
findings.quote: While retained business rates are revenue, this funding is replacing £12m of grant which is currently designated as capital.

findings.paper_title: Draft Budget 202728 and Medium-Term Financial Plan 2027-2031 and Annual Business Plan Outline 202728
findings.headline: Bus fleet purchase adds £27m of capital expenditure across 2027/28 and 2028/29, with higher forecast borrowing costs
findings.detail: The delivery plan assumes the authority will buy and own the bus fleet for the Peterborough network. The paper says that borrowing for fleet, depot or network enhancement would not go ahead until a business case showing long-term affordability is approved. Total bus reform capital is put at £73m for 2027/28 to 2029/30, against £17m of bus capital grants over the same period.
findings.matters: A lender or finance director can see a council taking on borrowing to own transport assets for a franchised network, and the paper ties this to a funding gap.
findings.figures: £27m additional capital expenditure across 2027/28 and 2028/29; £73m bus reform capital 2027/28 to 2029/30; £17m bus services capital grants in the same period
findings.quote: The result of this is an additional £27m capital expenditure across 2027/28 and 2028/29 with a corresponding increase in forecast borrowing costs.

findings.paper_title: Draft Budget 202728 and Medium-Term Financial Plan 2027-2031 and Annual Business Plan Outline 202728
findings.headline: Draft MTFP sets aside the £4.95m current-year treasury management surplus in an earmarked reserve
findings.detail: The paper says this transfer is made to offset the short-term pressure from increased fleet borrowing and phased franchising. It is a one-off set-aside of a surplus rather than an ongoing income line.
findings.matters: A finance director can see a treasury surplus being used to cover a service deficit rather than returned to general reserves, which is a choice that other councils with franchising or transport pressures may face.
findings.figures: £4.95m treasury management surplus in the current year; £4.95m transferred to earmarked reserve
findings.quote: the draft MTFP assumes that the £4.95m surplus on treasury management activities in the current year are set aside in an earmarked reserve.

findings.paper_title: Draft Budget 202728 and Medium-Term Financial Plan 2027-2031 and Annual Business Plan Outline 202728
findings.headline: Passenger transport operational reserves projected at £3.25m at end of 2030/31, £5.1m below the 10% level the paper considers prudent
findings.detail: The draft MTFP sets aside the current-year treasury surplus in an earmarked reserve to offset the borrowing and phasing pressures. The paper says further income or cost decisions are needed to put the service on a prudent footing, and that options are being explored, including a higher Transport Levy and a network review.
findings.matters: A reader can see the reserve position that remains after the transfer, and what the authority says it will do to close the gap.
findings.figures: £3.25m operational reserves at end of 2030/31; £5.1m below the prudent level; prudent level set at 10% of operational (non-staffing, non-borrowing) costs; £4.95m treasury surplus set aside
findings.quote: Doing so leaves the service with operational reserves of £3.25m at the end of 2030/31, which is £5.1m lower than the 10% of operational (non-staffing, non-borrowing) costs considered prudent

findings.paper_title: Draft Budget 202728 and Medium-Term Financial Plan 2027-2031 and Annual Business Plan Outline 202728
findings.headline: Revised bus franchising delivery plan creates a £14.1m pressure to the end of 2029/30 against last year's MTFP
findings.detail: The paper compares the revised delivery plan with the forecasts in last year's medium-term financial plan. A £10.6m fall in expenditure in 2028/29 is more than offset by an £18.9m fall in forecast fare income, because two lots of routes stay deregulated and outside the authority's finances until later.
findings.matters: A finance officer elsewhere can compare how a phased franchising plan shifts costs and income between years, and how a plan change shows up against the previous year's forecast.
findings.figures: £14.1m pressure to end of 2029/30; £10.6m decrease in anticipated expenditure in 2028/29; £18.9m reduction in forecast fare income; net variance £8,278k in 2028/29 and £8,006k in 2029/30
findings.quote: What the above shows is that the revised delivery plan creates a pressure of £14.1m to the end of 2029/30 compared to the forecasts including in last year's MTFP.

findings.paper_title: Draft Budget 202728 and Medium-Term Financial Plan 2027-2031 and Annual Business Plan Outline 202728
findings.headline: Franchised bus revenue budget shows a £9.47m deficit in 2028/29, reducing to £7.22m in 2029/30 and a £3.57m surplus in 2030/31
findings.detail: The paper attributes the deficit to the introduction of the franchised network and associated borrowing charges. Fare income offsets part of the rising operating expenditure but does not fully cover it. These are forecast positions rather than actual results.
findings.matters: A finance director or lender can see the bus service moving from a multi-year deficit to a forecast surplus, and that the timing depends on franchising rolling out in phases through 2030.
findings.figures: £9.47m deficit in 2028/29; £7.22m deficit in 2029/30; £3.57m surplus in 2030/31; network expenditure £78.10m by 2030/31; minimum revenue provision and interest £3.78m in 2028/29; fare income £53.48m in 2030/31
findings.quote: The forecast deficit rises to £9.47m in 2028/29, before reducing to £7.22m in 2029/30 and moving to a projected £3.57m surplus in 2030/31.

findings.matters: Per-scheme award limits delegated to officers, with a Subsidy Control Assessment as a condition, set out how a grant programme of this kind is controlled, which other finance officers may want to compare with their own delegation arrangements.

findings.detail: The paper recommends approval of the Full Business Case and £26,660,696 for the programme, following consideration by the Funding Committee on 2 November 2026. The sum is a capital grant commitment, and the paper describes a Wave 1 pipeline and a Wave 2 prospectus alongside it.

A draft Annual Business Plan is due before publication early next financial year.
findings.matters: A development body funded through a partner agency's service level agreement, with its resourcing model still open, is a funding arrangement a finance director may need to track when planning shared or delegated delivery.

findings.detail: The funding was awarded through a competitive national process, with up to ten new areas selected for the second phase. It will support work with young people aged 14–25, particularly those who are not in education, employment or training.
findings.matters: It is a specific grant won through a competitive process, with a stated two-year profile that finance officers at other councils can compare against their own grant assumptions.

findings.detail: The report lists this among the Budget measures relevant to the Combined Authority, alongside £11.09 million of seed funding for a Good Growth Fund and £150m of increased capacity funding. The report also notes a Fiscal Devolution Roadmap that includes future income tax assignment.
findings.matters: A new ring-fenced borrowing facility for all Mayoral Strategic Authorities changes the borrowing options available to peer authorities as well as this one.

findings.headline: The Future Funding risk is updated to reflect the current position on fiscal devolution from April 2027.
findings.detail: The paper reports that the Future Funding risk has been updated, with the wording tied to the current position on fiscal devolution. The paper gives April 2027 as the date from which fiscal devolution applies.
findings.matters: Fiscal devolution from a fixed date changes how a combined authority funds itself, which is a reference point for finance directors planning income across the sector.
findings.figures: April 2027
findings.quote: to reflect the current position regarding fiscal devolution from April 2027.

findings.headline: The Peterborough Station Quarter risk description is strengthened to cover Peterborough City Council's involvement and reputational risk to the CPCA.
findings.detail: The paper reports a revised description of the PSQ risk, adding the involvement of Peterborough City Council and the reputational risks to the CPCA. The PSQ deep dive is shown in the schedule as deferred from June 2026.
findings.matters: Where a combined authority's reputational exposure on a capital project depends on a partner council's role, the revised wording shows how the risk has been redefined, which lenders and peer finance teams look at.
findings.figures: PSQ deep dive deferred from June 2026
findings.quote: Strengthening the description of the involvement of Peterborough City Council and the associated reputational risks to the CPCA in respect of the Peterborough Station Quarter project.

findings.headline: The Cyber Security risk has increased following the PHP exploitation but remains within appetite.
findings.detail: The risk was reviewed after the PHP exploitation and at the Board's request in September 2026. Controls were updated to reference leavers and movers processes and to cover third-party suppliers, including contract assessments, supplier liability and access controls.
findings.matters: The paper shows a cyber risk rising after a named vulnerability while still inside appetite, and it adds third-party supplier liability controls that other councils' contract teams may be reviewing.
findings.figures: none stated
findings.quote: Whilst overall the risk has increased, it currently remains within appetite.

findings.headline: The Resilience risk's likelihood score is reduced from 4 to 3 on progress in controls, while its impact score is raised from 3 to 4.
findings.detail: The paper reports that the likelihood score has fallen because of progress in implementing controls. The impact score has risen because, the paper says, any occurrence would have a major impact irrespective of controls.
findings.matters: A risk whose likelihood falls while its impact rises shows how the authority is re-weighting controls against consequence, which peers reviewing regional infrastructure and water risk would find useful.
findings.figures: likelihood score 4 to 3; impact score 3 to 4
findings.quote: the likelihood score has reduced from 4 to 3, reflecting progress in implementing controls.

findings.headline: The Corporate Risk Register falls from 17 to 15 risks as two are closed, leaving 0 Very High, 5 High, 7 Medium and 3 Low risks
findings.detail: The Procurement Act compliance risk is closed because arrangements are now embedded in business-as-usual. The Equalities risk is closed after an internal audit confirmed effective procedures, with minor process improvements recommended. The register now holds 0 Very High, 5 High, 7 Medium and 3 Low risks.
findings.matters: Closing two compliance risks on the basis of embedded processes and audit assurance is a decision another council's finance or governance team could compare with its own procurement-compliance position.
findings.figures: 15 risks (0 Very High (Red), 5 High (Amber), 7 Medium (Yellow), 3 Low (Green)); reduction of two risks
findings.quote: There has been a reduction of two risks since the last report.

findings.headline: The Bus Reform Programme's residual risk score is 18 against a projects and programmes risk appetite of 17, one of the risks above appetite in the register.
findings.detail: The paper identifies the Bus Reform Programme as the one risk remaining above the Authority's risk appetite, with a residual score of 18 against an appetite of 17. The risk concerns delivery of the programme in line with the franchising scheme.
findings.matters: A franchising programme scoring above its stated appetite is a live delivery risk that a finance director at another council running a bus franchising scheme would want to compare against.
findings.figures: residual score 18; projects and programmes risk appetite 17
findings.quote: The residual score for this risk is 18 against a projects and programmes risk appetite of 17.

findings.headline: An audit adjustment moves £327k of Net Zero Accelerator expenditure from 2026/27 back into 2025/26.
findings.detail: The paper says this was found in the final stages of the 2025/26 audit. It adds £327k to the 2026/27 expenditure budget, matched by the ringfenced grant balance. The paper says this is a timing adjustment with no change in total income or expenditure. This follows an earlier £854k adjustment on the same programme.
findings.matters: A finance director would want to see audit timing adjustments on ringfenced grants and how they are matched to the grant balance, especially when a second adjustment follows an earlier one on the same programme.
findings.figures: £327k timing adjustment; earlier £854k adjustment on the same programme
findings.quote: During the final stages of the audit another adjustment was identified, whereby £327k of expenditure recognised in 2026/27 related to activity that was undertaken in 2025/26.

findings.headline: The Brownfield Housing Fund grant of £26.661m is conditional on a minimum of 870 homes being unlocked.
findings.detail: The paper says the grant is conditional on delivery of agreed outputs, milestones and spend profile, and that homes must start on site before 31 March 2031. It also gives an aspirational stretch target of up to 1,300 homes. The housing element of the Wisbech High Street scheme may be considered for this funding, but the paper says a shortfall will remain because grant per unit is limited.
findings.matters: A finance director would want the output conditions and start-on-site deadline attached to this MHCLG grant, since failing them affects the funding.
findings.figures: £26.661m full business case funding value; 870 homes minimum; 1,300 homes stretch target; start on site before 31 March 2031
findings.quote: The agreement with MHCLG is that a minimum of 870 homes will be unlocked (with an aspirational stretch target of up to 1,300 homes)

findings.headline: The Bus Franchising - CPCA PT Operations Team forecast overspend of £500k will be eliminated by a DfT-funded budget increase.
findings.detail: The overspend results from additional work on the revised franchising delivery plan. The paper says DfT funding for this purpose has been received, and the variance will be removed if the Board approves the budget increase in paragraph 7.9.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council running a bus franchising programme would want to know how the forecast overspend is being matched to ringfenced government funding.
findings.figures: £500k forecast overspend; £500k DfT Bus Franchising Support Fund
findings.quote: this variance will be eliminated as the budget will be increased to match forecast expenditure

findings.headline: The Growth Hub Team underspend of £250k is being returned to the general fund because the export programme is now delivered nationally by DBT.
findings.detail: The paper states that locally funded delivery is no longer required, so the budget will go back to the general fund and be considered in the medium-term financial plan setting. Place and Economy as a whole is forecast £1.377m below budget.
findings.matters: A budget being released because a national programme has taken over a local activity is a specific example of the funding being returned rather than spent.
findings.figures: £250k Growth Hub underspend; Place and Economy forecast variance £1.377m against annual budget £36.641m
findings.quote: There is also £250k underspend on Growth Hub Team relating to the planned delivery of an export programme which is now being delivered via the national programme run by DBT.

findings.headline: Peterborough Station Quarter capital slippage of £6.773m is attributed to archaeological delays.
findings.detail: The paper identifies this as the most significant single project slippage in the Transport capital programme. A large year-to-date underspend on the project is described as the result of delays in receiving and processing claims, alongside the slippage.
findings.matters: A finance director elsewhere managing a large station or regeneration scheme would want to see the size of this slippage and the stated cause, which is an external site condition rather than a funding problem.
findings.figures: £6.773m slippage
findings.quote: The most significant of these is Peterborough Station Quarter where delays due to archaeological have result in slippage of £6.773m.

findings.headline: Forecast slippage on approved capital budgets is £12.008m, and a further £41.286m of Subject to Approval budgets is no longer expected to be spent in-year.
findings.detail: The paper reports that the forecast on approved capital budgets has fallen by £8.867m since Quarter 1, mostly due to Transport slippage. Year-to-date actual capital spend is £37.732m against a forecast outturn of £95.028m. The paper says the Subject to Approval budgets are being reprofiled through the SAF process and the MTFP.
findings.matters: Large capital slippage alongside a higher treasury income forecast shows how the timing of capital delivery is affecting the Authority's cash position and reported budget position.
findings.figures: £12.008m approved capital slippage; £41.286m STA budgets not expected in-year; £8.867m reduction in forecast since Quarter 1; £37.732m year-to-date actual; £95.028m forecast outturn
findings.quote: The forecast slippage on the approved capital budgets is £12.008m, with a further £41.286m of STA budgets no longer expected to be spent in-year.

findings.headline: Treasury management income is forecast £4.957m above budget, with the forecast up £0.686m since Quarter 1.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the overachievement to cash balances being higher than expected because capital spend has been delayed, and to new funding being received ahead of spend. It also says the Authority is earning a higher rate than anticipated on its liquidity balances. The paper states the overachievement is intended to support passenger transport cost pressures from 2027/28.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council would see treasury income rising as a result of capital slippage, and a lender would see that the income depends on cash balances and interest rates staying where they are.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Key Assumptions for the Draft 2728 MTFP
findings.headline: Income Tax retention is confirmed for April 2028, but it is not reflected in the MTFP because the details are not yet known.

findings.matters: A confirmed but unquantified income stream means the plan's future funding picture is incomplete, which other councils planning for devolved taxes would need to account for.

findings.detail: The paper says work is underway to enable the transition and that further details will be brought forward in a timely manner. It also says the MTFP narrative and budget tables will be updated once the financial impact is confirmed.
findings.matters: A new statutory responsibility with unquantified costs is a gap in the plan that finance directors at similar authorities would expect to see resolved before budget setting.
findings.quote: The Combined Authority will be taking on Police and Fire responsibilities from April 2028.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Key Assumptions for the Draft 2728 MTFP
findings.headline: The transport levy is assumed to rise by 4% in 2027/28, then by 2% a year in other years, with a 1% Tiger Pass uplift maintained from 2026/27.

findings.figures: 4% (2027/28), 2% p.a. (other years), 1% Tiger Pass uplift

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Key Assumptions for the Draft 2728 MTFP
findings.headline: The draft MTFP assumes no borrowing to fund the capital programme outside bus franchising.
findings.detail: The paper states that no borrowing outside bus franchising will fund the capital programme. It separately includes Peterborough Depot fleet acquisition costs, including capital expenditure and borrowing costs, within the passenger transport assumptions.
findings.matters: A stated borrowing limit tied to one programme is a clear constraint that lenders and finance directors would check against future capital plans.
findings.quote: No borrowing outside bus franchising (see below) to fund Capital programme.

findings.matters: A finance director or lender would want to know which recurring grant is being swapped for a tax-based income stream, since the two carry different volatility and risk.

findings.paper_title: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority Audit Results Report 2025-26

findings.paper_title: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority Audit Results Report 2025-26

findings.detail: The auditor says the Authority may have limited control over when third parties submit claims. Expenditure and funding were not always recognised in the correct accounting period as a result.
findings.matters: Grant claims submitted late by partners can move income into the wrong year, which affects any council relying on in-year grant income.
findings.quote: We also identified multiple cut-off issues arising from the late recognition of grants, due to the timing of grant submissions by counterparties

findings.paper_title: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority Audit Results Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Auditor rated working papers and supporting evidence 'Requires improvement' for 2025/26.
findings.detail: The auditor says most working papers were of a good standard, but some initial evidence did not meet the evidence matrix. Follow-up queries were sometimes overlooked or delayed, and the auditor recommends annotated submissions and internal review before submission.
findings.matters: Slow evidence handling is a common cause of audit delay, and other finance teams will want to see how the auditor rates it against the agreed timetable.
findings.quote: However, some initial evidence provided did not meet the requirements of our evidence matrix.

findings.paper_title: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority Audit Results Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Auditor raised three new control recommendations in 2025/26 and carried forward three from prior years.
findings.detail: The Section 04 recommendations cover the audit findings on controls, including the journal authorisation gap. The table records four open matters at the date of the report.
findings.matters: A count of open audit recommendations and their age is a standard indicator of control maturity that another council's audit committee would compare.
findings.figures: New recommendations in 2025/26: 3; carried forward from prior years: 3; total open matters: 4
findings.quote: Section 04 sets out the details of the three recommendations raised in the year together with an update on the implementation status of the three recommendations carried forward from prior years.

findings.paper_title: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority Audit Results Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Auditor identified no matters requiring reporting by exception on financial sustainability, governance, or economy, efficiency and effectiveness.
findings.detail: The value for money work is complete and the auditor found no significant weaknesses in arrangements for any of the three criteria. No matters are to be reported by exception in the audit opinion.
findings.matters: A clean value for money conclusion is the result a finance director elsewhere will benchmark against when assessing their own financial sustainability risk.
findings.quote: We have not identified any matters requiring reporting by exception in relation to significant weaknesses in financial sustainability, governance, or economy, efficiency and effectiveness.

findings.paper_title: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority Audit Results Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Management corrected £1.48 million of misstatements and left £0.57 million uncorrected.

findings.matters: A finance director comparing audit adjustment volumes with peers will look at the split between corrected and uncorrected amounts.

findings.quote: Uncorrected misstatements amounting to £0.57 million

findings.headline: Net pension asset of £7.18 million at 31 March 2026 was limited to nil under IFRIC 14.
findings.detail: The auditor says the Authority's share of the Cambridgeshire Pension Fund investments exceeds its liability, but the asset is capped at nil under the accounting requirements. The auditor is still awaiting the pension fund auditor's findings.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council with a surplus in its pension fund share will need to know the asset ceiling applies, since it affects the balance sheet.

findings.paper_title: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority Audit Results Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Authority holds £62.79 million of Long-Term Investments in the Balance Sheet, relating to loans to subsidiary companies.
findings.detail: The auditor treated recoverability of these loans as a risk area and tested the assumptions and sensitivities used in impairment calculations. Two £0.15 million valuation differences were corrected by management, one increasing and one decreasing the valuation of individual subsidiaries.
findings.matters: Councils that lend to their own companies carry this exposure on the balance sheet, and a lender or finance director will want to see the size and the recoverability testing.
findings.figures: Long-Term Investments: £62.79 million; valuation differences: £0.15 million each
findings.quote: As at 31 March 2026 the Authority holds Long-Term Investments of £62.79 million in the Balance Sheet in relation to the loans issued to subsidiary companies.

findings.paper_title: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority Audit Results Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Two property valuations exceeded the auditor's supportable range, with overstatements of £0.29 million and £0.27 million.
findings.detail: The auditor's valuation specialist attributed the difference mainly to rent-free periods in existing leases, which the Authority's specialist did not reflect because it assumed vacant possession. Both overstatements are reported as unadjusted differences.
findings.matters: Valuation assumptions that ignore lease terms are a method issue other councils holding investment or University-related property will want to check against their own valuers' instructions.

findings.paper_title: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority Audit Results Report 2025-26

It also found a third-party claim that included expenditure incurred before 1 April 2025, which the Authority had not known about.

findings.detail: The auditor raised this as a control weakness under the presumed risk of management override of controls. It says it found no instances where the gap led to management override.
findings.matters: Manual journal authorisation is a standard control that other councils' audit committees will ask about, and a missing procedure is a point the auditor has put in writing.

findings.figures: Deadline: 30 June 2026
findings.quote: The financial statements were published by the 30 June 2026 deadline set out in the Accounts and Audit Regulations.

findings.detail: The paper lists the authority's larger number of counterparties and lower bail-in exposure as positives in its benchmarking against similar entities. It presents both as favourable features of the portfolio.

findings.matters: A lender or finance director can see that this authority's counterparty risk is reported as marginally higher than the sector average, alongside higher returns.

It says taking money out at an inopportune time could lead to significant losses, so investment in those funds has not been considered appropriate.

findings.paper_title: Appendix C: Corporate Risk Heatmap & Residual Movement
findings.headline: Corporate risk CRR0002 on future funding uncertainty and financial planning has a residual score of 13 (Medium) at each review from 02/26 to 08/26, down from 22 (Very High) at 11/25.
findings.detail: The paper's score history shows CRR0002 at Very High (22) in the 11/25 review and Medium (13) at the 02/26, 05/26 and 08/26 reviews. The current residual priority is Medium (13) and the inherent priority is High (17). The target rating in the heat map is Medium.
findings.matters: A finance director at this or another council would want to know when the council's own assessment of funding uncertainty for its financial planning has moved, and by how much.
findings.figures: Residual score 22 (Very High) at 11/25; residual score 13 (Medium) at 02/26, 05/26 and 08/26; inherent score 17 (High).
findings.quote: Future Funding uncertainty and impact on financial planning

findings.paper_title: Final accounts A&G covering report Nov 2026
findings.headline: Valuations of subsidiary companies were updated in the final accounts after their own accounts were finalised, and the change is recorded as an adjusted difference in the auditor's report.
findings.detail: The draft accounts published on 30 June 2026 had outstanding work on subsidiary valuations because the subsidiaries' accounts were not yet final. The paper says the final accounts reflect the updated figures.
findings.matters: Valuation timing for subsidiaries is a recurring point where published draft and final figures can diverge, which matters to anyone reading group accounts.
findings.quote: These have been updated in the final accounts and noted as an adjusted difference in the auditor’s report.

findings.paper_title: Final accounts A&G covering report Nov 2026
findings.headline: The Annual Governance Statement was amended after EY comments to state that no material governance weaknesses were identified in the year.
findings.detail: The paper says one paragraph of the Annual Governance Statement was updated to say more explicitly that no material governance weaknesses were identified. The change followed EY's comments.
findings.matters: A governance statement that the auditor has explicitly reviewed for wording is a point finance directors may compare when assessing their own governance disclosures.
findings.quote: one paragraph in the Annual Governance Statement has been updated to more explicitly state that no material governance weaknesses were identified in the year.

findings.paper_title: Final accounts A&G covering report Nov 2026
findings.headline: The auditor's draft report anticipates a qualified opinion again for 2026/27, with an unqualified opinion possible for 2027/28.
findings.detail: The paper reports the auditor's expectation that assurance will improve in 2026/27 but still produce a qualified opinion. The Combined Authority says it wants to discuss with the auditors whether a return to unqualified opinions can happen earlier.
findings.matters: Finance directors and lenders can use this forward timetable to judge when the qualification is expected to fall away across the sector.
findings.figures: 2026/27 expected qualified; 2027/28 unqualified possible
findings.quote: The Auditor’s draft report indicates that they anticipate that assurance will improve again in 2026/27, but still result in a qualified opinion, with a return to an unqualified opinion being possible for the 2027/28 accounts.

findings.paper_title: Final accounts A&G covering report Nov 2026
findings.headline: All 21 areas in the auditor's Summary of Assurances now have substantial assurance, up from 17 areas for the 2024/25 audit.
findings.detail: The paper reports that no material issues were identified in the 2025/26 work. It also says the auditor was able to perform substantive testing on transactions, which it could not do for 2022/23.
findings.matters: Movement from 17 to 21 substantial assurance areas in a single year is a measurable indicator that a finance director and lenders can compare with peers.
findings.figures: 21 areas with substantial assurance; 17 areas for 2024/25
findings.quote: all 21 of the areas within the ‘Summary of Assurances’ table on p40-42 now having substantial assurance, up from 17 for the 2024/25 audit.

findings.paper_title: Final accounts A&G covering report Nov 2026
findings.headline: EY issues a qualified opinion on the Combined Authority's 2025/26 accounts, the first audit opinion the Authority has received since 2022/23, with the qualification tied to carried-forward balances.
findings.detail: The paper says the qualification arises from the national audit backstop issues, not from identified errors in the accounts. The auditor could not gain assurance over the 2022/23 closing balances, which carry forward into later years.
findings.matters: A finance director at another authority affected by the backstop process will see how a qualified opinion is being explained and what the route back to an unqualified opinion looks like.
findings.figures: Qualified opinion; first opinion since 2022/23
findings.quote: This opinion is qualified only due to the impact of carried forward balances lacking assurance as a result of the national audit issues identified earlier.

findings.headline: Future Funding risk updated to reflect the position on fiscal devolution from April 2027.
findings.detail: The Future Funding risk has been revised in the register to reflect the current position on fiscal devolution. The paper gives no figures for the change.
findings.matters: Fiscal devolution from April 2027 changes how combined authorities are funded, so finance officers at other devolved authorities will be tracking the same risk.
findings.figures: April 2027
findings.quote: Future Funding which has been updated to reflect the current position regarding fiscal devolution from April 2027.

findings.headline: Cyber security risk raised following the PHP exploitation, and remains within appetite.
findings.detail: The Cyber Security risk was reviewed after the PHP exploitation and at the request of the Combined Authority Board. The paper says the risk has increased overall but is still within appetite, and that its position will be kept under review.
findings.matters: Councils and combined authorities are reviewing cyber exposure after the same PHP exploitation, so how this authority scored its risk is a comparison point for peers.
findings.quote: Whilst overall the risk has increased, it currently remains within appetite.

findings.headline: Corporate Risk Register holds 15 risks, a reduction of two since the last report.
findings.detail: The register now has no Very High risks, 5 High, 7 Medium and 3 Low. The two closures are the Procurement Act risk and an equalities legislation risk, which the paper says an internal audit found to be effectively mitigated.
findings.matters: Changes in the number and rating of corporate risks show how a council's risk position is moving over time, which peers and lenders compare.
findings.figures: 15 risks; 0 Very High (Red); 5 High (Amber); 7 Medium (Yellow); 3 Low (Green); reduction of 2 risks
findings.quote: There has been a reduction of two risks since the last report.

findings.headline: Procurement Act compliance risk closed, as compliance arrangements are now embedded within business-as-usual operations and processes
findings.detail: The Procurement Act compliance risk has been removed from the register. The paper says compliance arrangements are now part of routine operations and processes.
findings.matters: Procurement Act compliance is a common pressure across councils, and a finance director at a peer authority may want to know how this one has closed its risk.
findings.quote: This risk has been closed, as compliance arrangements are now embedded within business-as-usual operations and processes.

findings.headline: Bus Reform Programme risk sits above appetite, with a residual score of 18 against an appetite of 17.
findings.detail: The paper identifies the Bus Reform Programme as the one risk above the Authority's risk appetite. The risk is that the programme may not be delivered in line with the franchising scheme.
findings.matters: A franchising programme scored above appetite is a governance signal that other councils running bus reform will want to compare against their own risk registers.
findings.figures: Residual score 18; projects and programmes risk appetite 17 (score points)
findings.quote: The residual score for this risk is 18 against a projects and programmes risk appetite of 17.

findings.headline: Combined Authority expects interest rates to rise this year, reversing earlier forecasts of cuts in 2026 and 2027
findings.detail: The paper states that rates have stayed higher than anticipated and are now expected to increase further in 2026/27. It says a revised forecast will go to the November CPCA Board and be built into the 2027/28 medium-term financial plan.
findings.matters: A finance director would see a change in the rate outlook that feeds directly into the treasury forecasts and medium-term budget assumptions their own council may be revising.
findings.quote: interest rates have remained higher than was anticipated and are now expected to increase further this year when earlier forecasts had costed in rate cuts in 2026 and 2027.

findings.headline: Combined Authority says the integration of Police and Fire from May 2028 adds uncertainty to its treasury planning
findings.detail: The paper says work on understanding Police and Fire's arrangements and treasury positions is at a very early stage, and that the corporate cashflow operating model has not yet been determined. This uncertainty is used to justify not seeking to increase longer-term limits in the 2027/28 strategy.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council facing a similar multi-service integration would see how the treasury limits and cashflow model are being held back until the operating model is settled.
findings.quote: the integration of Police and Fire from May 2028.

findings.headline: Combined Authority has reached its agreed limit for longer-term investments extending beyond the financial year-end
findings.detail: The paper says the limit for longer-term deals beyond year-end was reached from the end of September, as it was also in 2025/26. It states that the 2027/28 Treasury Strategy is unlikely to increase that limit, citing uncertainty around the Police and Fire integration.
findings.matters: A finance director would see a counterparty or duration limit being hit for a second consecutive year, which limits their ability to lock in longer-term rates when they are available.
findings.quote: since the end of September, we have reached the agreed limit for longer term that extend beyond the financial year-end, which we also reached during 2025/26.

findings.headline: Combined Authority reports no breaches of its agreed treasury and capital indicators in 2026/27
findings.detail: The paper states that performance against the indicators agreed in the 2026/27 strategies is set out in Appendix A, and that none of the indicators were breached during the year.
findings.matters: A finance director would note a clean indicator position at mid-year, which is a standard assurance point they compare against their own treasury reporting.
findings.quote: There have been no breaches of the agreed indicators during 2026/27.

findings.headline: Forecast Treasury Investment balance at year end will exceed the £50.9m indicator figure
findings.detail: The paper says the delay to bus franchising capital spend and other programme slippage will push the year-end Treasury Investment balance above the forecast set in Indicator 11.
findings.matters: Higher year-end investment balances from capital slippage are a reserve-like cash position that a finance director would track against their own liquidity and investment plans.
findings.figures: £50.9m forecast Treasury Investment balance at year end (Indicator 11)
findings.quote: the forecast £50.9m Treasury Investment balance at year end, in Indicator 11, will be considerably exceeded.

findings.headline: Bus franchising debt-funded capital investment moves to 2027/28 under a three-phase implementation
findings.detail: Debt-funded capital investment for bus franchising was expected during 2026/27 when the indicators were set. The paper says the shift to a three-phase implementation means it is now expected to commence in 2027/28, which the paper says will lead to large favourable variances in the financing requirement and debt indicators.
findings.matters: A finance director would see a capital scheme slipping a year and reducing in-year borrowing, which affects their own capital programme phasing and borrowing forecasts.
findings.figures: Financing requirement and debt indicators 9 and 10 show large favourable variances against the start-of-year forecast
findings.quote: this is now expected to commence in 2027/28.

findings.headline: Combined Authority forecasts £8.9m in-year treasury income, £4.2m above the budget set at the start of the year
findings.detail: The paper attributes the higher income to larger investment balances and to interest rates staying higher than anticipated. It reports that rates are now expected to rise further this year, where earlier forecasts had assumed cuts in 2026 and 2027.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council would see a treasury income overachievement of this size against budget, driven by the timing of capital spend and by rates, which is the kind of variance their own mid-year monitoring may be picking up.
findings.figures: £8.9m total forecast in-year income; £4.2m overachievement against budget
findings.quote: is currently forecasting a total in-year income of £8.9m – a £4.2m overachievement vs the budget set at the start of the year.

findings.paper_title: Budget and Annual Business Plan Working Group Report 2026
findings.headline: The working group asks the Combined Authority to ensure future borrowing for major transport investment and franchising is supported by asset management and financial planning.
findings.detail: The recommendation links future borrowing decisions to asset registration, valuation, depreciation, lifecycle management and internal cost allocation. It asks for a clear understanding of service viability and long-term affordability before borrowing is committed.
findings.matters: Borrowing tied to franchising assets with no defined asset management framework is a question that lenders and finance directors at other combined authorities would expect to see answered.
findings.figures: None stated
findings.quote: ensuring that future borrowing decisions associated with major transport investments and franchising are supported by robust asset management and financial planning arrangements

findings.paper_title: Budget and Annual Business Plan Working Group Report 2026
findings.headline: Members heard concerns that the Combined Authority is comparatively under-resourced against other Mayoral Strategic Authorities, with a relatively small transport team supporting a significant programme of work.
findings.detail: The working group recommended that the Board recognise current capacity constraints and consider proposals to strengthen in-house transport and infrastructure capability. It also asked for a review of the balance between internal staff and external consultants, including where consultancy may not be the most cost-effective approach.
findings.matters: Heavy reliance on consultants for major capital delivery is a cost and accountability question that finance officers at other councils face when planning large schemes.
findings.figures: None stated
findings.quote: The Committee heard concerns that the CPCA remains comparatively under-resourced when measured against other Mayoral Strategic Authorities

findings.paper_title: Budget and Annual Business Plan Working Group Report 2026
findings.headline: Government capacity funding for devolution has been provided on a one-off basis, and the paper describes it as remaining limited.
findings.detail: Officers noted that additional capacity funding has been provided by Government to support devolution. The working group heard that this funding is one-off and that its amount is limited.
findings.matters: One-off devolution capacity funding raises the question of how recurring staffing and capability costs will be met, which peer finance directors and lenders would track.
findings.figures: None stated
findings.quote: While additional capacity funding has been provided by Government, this is on a one-off basis and remains limited.

findings.paper_title: Budget and Annual Business Plan Working Group Report 2026
findings.headline: The Combined Authority continues to rely primarily on grant funding because it has no tax base of its own.
findings.detail: Officers told the Resources session that the authority's income is mainly grant-based. Officers also said national discussions on retaining a share of business rates and other fiscal levers are ongoing, with future arrangements subject to Government decisions.
findings.matters: Income that depends almost entirely on central government grant is a structural feature a lender or peer finance officer would weigh when assessing the authority's financial resilience.
findings.figures: None stated
findings.quote: The authority continues to rely primarily on grant funding due to the absence of its own tax base.

findings.paper_title: Budget and Annual Business Plan Working Group Report 2026
findings.headline: Officers say funding for the Peterborough bus franchising depot is subject to approval, and that its omission from current forecasts will be checked, with around £5 million previously identified as provision.
findings.detail: Members asked whether provision for the depot was included in current financial forecasts. Officers said the omission would be checked and that an estimated provision had previously been identified. Officers also confirmed that further depot capacity will be required as franchising expands.
findings.matters: A large transport asset that may be missing from the forecast, with funding not yet approved, is the kind of gap a finance director would want to know about and a lender would want to see resolved.
findings.figures: around £5 million
findings.quote: Officers advised that funding for the depot was subject to approval and that the omission would be checked, with an estimated provision of around £5 million having previously been identified.

findings.headline: Transport income of £39m received to date in 2026/27, with the full-year forecast in line with the £86,531k budget
findings.detail: The paper reports that income to date is in line with expectations and that the forecast outturn matches the expected budget. The Transport Levy income line is £1,079k ahead of its year-to-date budget.
findings.matters: Income forecast on budget at the half-year point, with a levy line running ahead of profile, is a position finance officers at peer councils would compare with their own mid-year income tracking.
findings.figures: Total transport income FY budget £86,531k; FY forecast £86,531k; FY variance £0k; YTD actual £38,873k against YTD budget £37,791k; income to date £39m
findings.quote: The income received to date in the year is £39m in line with expectations.

findings.headline: Transport revenue expenditure at £7,702k year to date against a £10,221k budget, with the underspend attributed to a lag in contractor billing
findings.detail: The paper says most of the year-to-date underspend sits in public transport bus services because contractors' billing is lagging. The full-year forecast shows a £125k variance, from the Market Towns Cycle Support start being delayed and spread over three years.
findings.matters: Billing lags make year-to-date underspends look larger than the eventual outturn, which finance directors reviewing mid-year monitoring figures would need to allow for.
findings.figures: YTD actual £7,702k against YTD budget £10,221k; YTD variance -£2,519k; FY budget £23,831k; FY forecast £23,706k; FY variance -£125k
findings.quote: the underspend here is because of a lag in billing from contractors

findings.headline: Road Safety Fund capital forecast at £150k against a £590k budget, with the variance attributed to delays in agreeing the Grant Funding Agreement
findings.detail: The paper says the variance reflects timing changes and rescheduled resource, following delays in agreeing the grant funding legal document. A revised agreement is now being agreed. Year-to-date spend is nil against a £120k budget.
findings.matters: Grant-funded programmes whose spend depends on a legal agreement being finalised are exposed to the same delay, and finance teams elsewhere would want to see how long that step takes.
findings.figures: FY budget £590k; FY forecast £150k; FY variance -£440k; deferral £440k; YTD budget £120k
findings.quote: delays in agreeing the Grant Funding Agreement (GFA) legal document

findings.headline: March junction improvements forecast at £4,914k against a £5,321k budget, with a two-year extension to 2028/29 sought to fund Hostmoor Avenue
findings.detail: The paper attributes the underspend to efficiencies and a revised traffic-management approach on the A141 / Twenty Foot Road works, and to NILR detailed design not progressing. Approval is being sought to use the underspend for Hostmoor Avenue and to extend the funding and delivery period, with no intended increase in CPCA funding.
findings.matters: Re-using an underspend on a funded scheme and extending its delivery period, without new CPCA money, is a reprofiling decision that finance officers managing similar programme underspends would want to compare with their own approval routes.
findings.figures: FY budget £5,321k; FY forecast £4,914k; FY variance -£407k; YTD actual £1,882k against YTD budget £2,406k; extension from 2026/27 to 2028/29
findings.quote: to extend the funding/delivery period by two financial years from 2026/27 to 2028/29

findings.headline: A141 capital forecast at £1,800k against a £2,275k budget, with the variance attributed to refreshing the Outline Business Case for the High Growth scenario
findings.detail: The paper says the A141 and St Ives programme is being re-examined so the package responds to the High Growth scenario. The period will also cover consultation outcomes, surveys and technical work ahead of Preliminary Designs and the Full Business Case.
findings.matters: A scheme moving back to business case refresh before design work continues is a timing change that finance officers managing pre-construction spend on growth-linked schemes would want to see in their own profiles.
findings.figures: FY budget £2,275k; FY forecast £1,800k; FY variance -£475k; deferral £475k; YTD actual £453k
findings.quote: the Outline Business Case to consider how the package should evolve to respond to the High Growth scenario

findings.headline: LEVI capital forecast at £500k against a £3,000k budget, with £2,500k reprofiled over the following three years after a procurement change
findings.detail: The paper attributes the change to revised procurement to meet DfT expectations, with expenditure now expected to start in Q4 2026/27 and contract award anticipated during 2026/27. The remaining funding is to be reprofiled across three subsequent years, and DfT has been told of the revised profile.
findings.matters: A large grant-funded capital programme moving most of its spend into later years is a profile change that councils running similar EV infrastructure programmes would be tracking against their own grant conditions.
findings.figures: FY budget £3,000k; FY forecast £500k; FY variance -£2,500k; deferral £2,500k
findings.quote: Following changes to the procurement process to meet the expectations of the DfT, expenditure is now expected to commence from Q4 2026/27.

findings.headline: A10 upgrade capital forecast at £629k against a £1,259k budget, after DfT confirmed the A10 is no longer on its MRN/LLM list
findings.detail: The paper says DfT has told the Combined Authority the A10 will leave the Major Road Network list, and that expenditure is being deferred until there is greater clarity on funding. Year-to-date capital spend is £196k against a £498k budget.
findings.matters: A scheme losing its expected government funding route, with spend deferred and the deferral carried into later years, is a funding risk that finance officers elsewhere managing major-road schemes would want to track.
findings.figures: FY budget £1,259k; FY forecast £629k; FY variance -£630k; deferral £630k; YTD actual £196k against YTD budget £498k
findings.quote: The Combined Authority has now been informed by DfT that the A10 will no longer remain on its MRN/LLM list.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B - LVEP Business Plan Budget
findings.headline: The draft LVEP budget total rises from £65,000 in Yr 1 to £348,000 in Yr 5, with resource costs rising from £40,000 to £159,500 over the same period.
findings.detail: The TOTAL row gives yearly totals of £65,000, £238,000, £310,000, £343,000 and £348,000. The Resource line steps up from £40,000 in Yr 1 to £159,500 from Yr 4 onward, and the paper does not explain the increase.
findings.matters: The budget roughly quintuples over five years in a partnership that partner councils are being asked to fund, so a peer council would want to see the scale of the ramp before agreeing its contribution.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B - LVEP Business Plan Budget
findings.headline: Local authority contributions to the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough LVEP budget remain subject to approval through each organisation's medium-term financial planning and budget cycles.
findings.detail: The paper is marked as a draft for discussion. It also states that LVEP projects are subject to the CPCA's SAF Framework, so the budget lines are not yet approved by the partner councils.
findings.matters: A partner council's finance officer would need to know that its share of a shared budget has not yet been approved through its own budget cycle.
findings.figures: None stated
findings.quote: Please note Local Authority contributions remain subject to approval through each organisations Medium Term financial planning and budget cycles.

findings.headline: Revenue STA programmes forecast £1.9m below budget (16.4% shortfall)
findings.detail: STA revenue budget of £11.444m is forecast at £9.567m, a variance of -£1.877m. Spatial Development Strategy shows the largest underspend at £1.554m (full allocation forecast at zero). Other variances include Local Remediation Acceleration Plans (£166k forecast at zero), Active Travel revenue (£83k forecast at zero), and Rewilding Programme (£75k forecast from £150k budget). Core services and operational programmes remain on forecast.
findings.matters: Revenue programme underspends indicate non-progression on strategic initiatives or budget constraints; the Spatial Development Strategy underspend is material as planning strategy underpins economic delivery
findings.figures: Revenue budget £11,444k, forecast £9,567k, variance -£1,877k. Spatial Development Strategy: £1,554k budgeted, £0 forecast. Local Remediation Plans: £166k budgeted, £0 forecast. Active Travel: £83k budgeted, £0 forecast. Rewilding: £150k budgeted, £75k forecast

findings.headline: Subject to Approval capital programmes forecast £44.3m below budget (58.7% shortfall)
findings.detail: The combined authority's STA capital budget for 2026/27 is £75.527m but Q1 forecasts only £31.234m expenditure, a variance of -£44.293m. Major contributors to the underspend include Bus Franchising Depot Improvements (£21m forecast at zero), Local Growth Plan Delivery Fund (£7.413m forecast at zero), Capital for Skills grant (£3.5m forecast at zero), Resilience Plan Capital Fund (£3.173m forecast at zero), and A10 Upgrade (£3m forecast at zero). Programmes remaining on forecast include transport operations, railway station development, and housing programmes.
findings.matters: Large forecast underspends indicate either delivery delays or grant funding shortfalls affecting capital deployment; finance directors assess capital delivery risk and lenders evaluate creditworthiness partly through infrastructure project delivery
findings.figures: Capital budget £75,527k, forecast £31,234k, variance -£44,293k. Bus Franchising Depot: £21,000k budgeted, £0 forecast. Local Growth Plan: £7,413k budgeted, £0 forecast. Capital for Skills: £3,500k budgeted, £0 forecast. Resilience Plan: £3,173k budgeted, £0 forecast. A10 Upgrade: £3,000k budgeted, £0 forecast

findings.headline: Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure capital programme reforecasted from £3.0m budget to £0.5m.
findings.detail: The Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure programme is forecast to deliver only £0.5m against a full-year budget of £3.0m, representing a £2.5m reduction (83% of budget). Year-to-date spend is £16k. Slippage of £2.5m is requested, indicating the authority expects to recover this in later quarters, but the scale of reforecasting suggests either a substantial delivery delay or programme rescoping.
findings.matters: A material downward revision of a transport decarbonisation capital scheme signals either delivery challenges or changed funding assumptions; the recovery trajectory needs monitoring.

findings.quote: Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure - 16 16 3,000 500 -2,500 -2,500 2,500

findings.headline: Investment income forecast at £8.9m, exceeding budget by £4.3m.
findings.detail: Investment income is forecast to deliver £8.9m against a budget of £4.7m, an upside of £4.3m (92% more than budgeted). Year-to-date actual of £2.4m in three months indicates an effective annual run rate of approximately £9.7m. findings.matters: Better-than-expected investment returns strengthen the authority's financial position and support reserves without requiring spending reductions or operational income growth.

findings.quote: Interest Receivable on Investments -2,433  -4,655 -8,926 -4,271  -4,271

findings.detail: The planned local delivery of the export programme under 'Team Cambridgeshire and Peterborough' is no longer required as it is now being delivered via the national programme run by the Department for Business and Trade. The £250k underspend will be returned to the general fund for use in the medium-term financial plan.
findings.matters: Changes to national programme delivery reduce local authority budget requirements and free resources for reallocation
findings.figures: Variance -£250k (Budget £789k, Forecast £539k)
