As locally funded delivery is no longer required, this budget will be returned to the general fund and considered within the overall setting of the medium-term financial plan

findings.headline: Resilience Plan Phase 2 and Health/Wellbeing Strategy development both deferred to 2027/28
findings.detail: The Resilience Plan has adopted a phased approach with Phase 1 commissioned and due to report in November 2026, while Phase 2 development is now scheduled for 2027/28. The Health/Wellbeing Strategy development was also deferred and is expected to complete in 2027/28, with current year spend focused on expert advice and system tools.
findings.matters: Significant programme slippage affects medium-term planning timelines and the phasing of capital allocation decisions
findings.figures: Resilience Plan variance -£300k, Health/Wellbeing Strategy variance -£300k (together £600k slippage)
findings.quote: Following decision by Growth Committee to take a phased approach to the Resilience Plan (with Phase 1 commissioned and due to report in November 2026) the Phase 2 development work will now take place in 2027/28

findings.headline: Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure programme defers £2.5m after DfT requires procurement process changes
findings.detail: The programme has revised its procurement process to meet Department for Transport expectations. Expenditure is now expected to commence from Q4 2026/27, with contract award anticipated during 2026/27. The remaining funding will be reprofiled across the subsequent three years.
findings.matters: Changes in government requirements for procurement delay major capital investment and shift funding across future years, affecting capital planning certainty
findings.figures: Variance -£2,500k (Budget £3,000k, Forecast £500k for 2026/27)
findings.quote: Following changes to the procurement process to meet the expectations of the DfT, expenditure is now expected to commence from Q4 2026/27.

findings.headline: A10 Upgrade programme defers £630k of expenditure pending government feedback on Major Road Network funding
findings.detail: The A10 programme has adopted a revised delivery profile, deferring elements of expenditure until receiving government feedback on the Major Road Network funding programme. The authority is continuing targeted activities to maintain momentum and preserve programme readiness.
findings.matters: Government funding decisions directly affect the timing and delivery of major capital projects, affecting both programme flow and funding certainty
findings.figures: Variance -£630k (Budget £1,259k, Forecast £629k for 2026/27)
findings.quote: The variance within the A10 programme is primarily due to a revised delivery profile while awaiting government feedback on the Major Road Network (MRN) funding programme.

findings.headline: Active Travel Officer post being advertised for third time as recruitment challenges delay Community Grant Scheme
findings.detail: The recruitment difficulty to the Active Travel Officer position is causing delays in the Community Grant Scheme delivery, with a £235,000 underspend. The position is currently being advertised for a third time, with expectation to successfully fill it during the current financial year.
findings.matters: Recruitment challenges delay service delivery and grant distribution, showing whether the authority can fill key posts to deliver programmes on time
findings.figures: £235,000 underspend in Community Grant Scheme; £551,000 total Active Travel programme variance
findings.quote: Delays in the delivery of the Community Grant Scheme have resulted in an underspend of £235,000. This is primarily due to the continued challenges in recruiting to the Active Travel Officer post, which is currently being advertised for a third time.

findings.headline: Youth Guarantee Trailblazer exceeded target with 146 young people engaged against 115-person target
findings.detail: Following recommissioning of core delivery partners, programme is performing strongly with 146 young people engaged against target of 115. All planned Year 2 commissioning activity completed with £1.5 million Interventions Fund awarded to 20 projects. Funding committed through 31 March 2027.
findings.matters: Shows strong program delivery and performance recovery after recommissioning. Exceeding targets indicates effective targeting and engagement. Committed funding through March 2027 provides spending visibility.
findings.figures: 146 engaged vs 115 target; £1.5 million fund; 20 projects commissioned; funding to 31 March 2027
findings.quote: Following the extension and recommissioning of core delivery partners during the first quarter of this financial year, the programme has continued to perform strongly, engaging 146 young people against a target of 115 for the period.

findings.headline: Impact assessment underway on £2 national bus fare cap extension to 31 December 2027
findings.detail: Government extended £2 cap on single bus fares outside London from original end date to 31 December 2027. Combined Authority is reviewing Tiger Pass scheme in this context, including financial and operational impacts. Findings will be reported to future Transport Committee and Board meetings once work concludes.
findings.matters: Government policy changes can create unexpected financial pressure or opportunity. Understanding implications for council-managed transport revenue is essential for budget planning.
findings.figures: £2 cap extended to 31 December 2027
findings.quote: Research is underway to assess the potential impact of this policy on passenger demand. The assessment will consider the implications for the Tiger Pass scheme, including financial and operational impacts.

findings.headline: £224 million homelessness funding approved with draft action plan due 1 December 2026
findings.detail: £224 million funding approved for homelessness work including support to end rough sleeping. For 2026/27, funding will be passported to Local Authorities with monitoring arrangements in place. Draft Homelessness Action Plan due 1 December 2026 will set framework for future spending and activity.
findings.matters: Represents significant new funding responsibility and budget area for the authority. Whether distributed through or managed by the authority, it creates financial and oversight obligations requiring budgeting and monitoring.
findings.figures: £224 million approved; draft plan deadline 1 December 2026
findings.quote: Funding of £224 million has been approved, with a key output being the development of a draft Homelessness Action Plan by 1 December 2026. This will provide the framework for future activity and investment, including additional funding to support the ambition to end rough sleeping.

findings.headline: £26.1 million Brownfield Land Fund Outline Business Case approved for housing delivery
findings.detail: Outline business case taken to Funding Committee for Brownfield Land Fund to support delivery of 870 homes. Approximately half of the £26.1m funding is profiled for year one. Homes supported must start on site by 2031.
findings.matters: Represents a significant capital investment program requiring financing and execution within defined timescale. Finance directors monitor capital deployment, funding requirements, and delivery progress.
findings.figures: £26.1 million programme; approximately £13m year one; 870 homes target; delivery by 2031
findings.quote: A Brownfield Land Fund Outline Business Case was taken to Funding Committee for a £26.1 million programme to support the delivery of 870 homes. Around half of the funding is profiled for year one, requiring the programme to move at pace and focus on deliverable sites.

findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation decision for Cambridgeshire and Peterborough paused and put under review
findings.detail: Secretary of State announced LGR decisions would be paused and reviewed. Decisions in four areas (Essex, Hampshire, Norfolk, Suffolk) were withdrawn entirely. Fourteen other areas, including Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, have decisions paused pending review. The Mayor and Officers continue working with government.
findings.matters: LGR decisions carry major financial implications including organizational restructuring, staffing changes, and service delivery redesign. Uncertainty about timing and outcome affects medium-term financial planning and creditworthiness.
findings.figures: 4 areas with decisions withdrawn; 14 areas paused including Cambridgeshire and Peterborough
findings.quote: Decisions in four areas were withdrawn, these included Essex, Hampshire, Norfolk and Suffolk; while fourteen other areas are to be reviewed and paused, this included Cambridgeshire and Peterborough.

findings.headline: Bloomberg Philanthropies programme securing circa £250k for data, digital and AI capacity over 18 months
findings.detail: Authority is tranche one of 18-month Bloomberg Philanthropies programme supporting Mayors and Strategic Authorities. Co-delivery through Inner Circle Consulting, London School of Economics, Public Digital and Portland Communications. Public Digital work specifically focused on enhancing data, digital and AI capabilities to support evidence-based decision making and delivery improvement. Anticipated £250k funding will support 2 FTE roles over 18-month period. Exact funding amount and mechanism to be confirmed.
findings.matters: External co-investment in strategic capability identified as area of organisational capacity and capability gap; demonstrates philanthropic interest in local government innovation and digital transformation; shows sector recognition of data and AI capability requirements.
findings.figures: Circa £250k funding (amount and mechanism pending confirmation); 2 FTE positions for 18-month period
findings.quote: It is anticipated that 2 FTE members of staff will be funded via Bloomberg Philanthropies for an 18 month period to support the Combined Authority drive forward a step change in data, digital and AI capabilities... This funding is anticipated to be circa £250k, with the exact amount and funding mechanism to be confirmed in the coming weeks.

findings.headline: MHCLG allocates £1.747m rough sleeping programme funding to authority for 2026/27, with provisional allocations for 2027-2029
findings.detail: MHCLG notification received 19 August 2026 allocating revenue funding for Rough Sleeping Programme for 2026/27, with provisional capital and revenue allocations for 2027/28 and 2028/29. Funding allocated across six local authorities using MHCLG Single Homelessness and Rough Sleeping formula, with largest allocations to Cambridge (£630,674) and Peterborough (£563,141). Provisional allocations: 2027/28 capital £1.423m, revenue £1.256m; 2028/29 capital £1.650m, revenue £1.270m.
findings.matters: New revenue stream devolved to authority; provides mechanism to deliver government commitment to end rough sleeping; creates multi-year funding visibility but also new governance, reporting and delivery accountability requirements for rough sleeping outcomes.
findings.figures: £1.747m 2026/27 allocation; provisional 2027/28 £1.423m capital and £1.256m revenue; provisional 2028/29 £1.650m capital and £1.270m revenue
findings.quote: On 19 August 2026 the Combined Authority received notification from MHCLG allocation of revenue funding for the Rough Sleeping Programme for 2026/27, with provisional revenue and capital allocations for 2027/28 and 2028/29.

findings.headline: Active Travel revenue programme underspending by £0.551m due to recruitment delays and programme delivery challenges
findings.detail: Forecast underspend of £0.551m on Active Travel Revenue Programme due to slippage into 2027/28. Root causes identified as challenges in recruitment to Active Travel Officer post and delays to Community Grant Scheme and Cycle Training programmes in Market Towns and Peterborough.
findings.matters: Reveals capacity constraints in delivering government-funded transport priorities; indicates staffing and HR challenges in specialist recruitment; demonstrates programme delivery risk in non-core service areas with specialist skill requirements.
findings.figures: £0.551m forecast underspend on Active Travel Revenue Programme
findings.quote: underspend of £0.551m on the Active Travel Revenue Programme which is due to slip into 2027/28 due to challenges in recruitment to the Active Travel Officer post along with delays to the Community Grant Scheme and Cycle Training programmes in Market Towns and Peterborough

findings.headline: £0.473m earmarked reserve drawdown approved for devolution response capacity
findings.detail: Board delegation approved for Chief Executive Officer to drawdown £0.473m from earmarked reserves for additional capacity to support response to government devolution agenda. Drawdown will only be made if required. Delegation also requested for Chief Finance Officer to include any future government capacity grant funding within authority budget if awarded.
findings.matters: Shows forward-looking response to government devolution agenda but creates reserve pressure if drawdown is needed; indicates recognition within finance function that forward resource investment is required ahead of formal funding confirmation; creates dependency on government delivering promised capacity grants.
findings.figures: £0.473m from earmarked reserves (set aside from previous underspending)
findings.quote: To delegate authority to the Chief Executive Officer to drawdown £0.473m from earmarked reserves for additional capacity to support the Authority's response to the Government's devolution agenda

findings.headline: Government devolution agenda will transfer substantial new responsibilities across multiple policy areas and governance functions
findings.detail: Government's 'Rewiring the State' agenda and authority's Established Mayoral Strategic Authority status confirmation signals significant acceleration in devolution. Proposed responsibility transfers include skills, employment support, transport, housing, planning, homelessness, fiscal devolution, public service integration, policing, fire governance and resilience, alongside enhanced accountability and governance requirements. Authority undertaking extensive preparatory work including policy development, capacity building, workforce planning, governance design and stakeholder engagement ahead of detailed funding confirmation.
findings.matters: Creates immediate and forward organisational capacity pressures and structural spending commitments; indicates multi-directorate implications and need for resource mobilization ahead of formal funding arrangements; represents strategic opportunity but also uncertainty about future cost and resource requirements.
findings.figures: Scope includes skills, employment support, transport, housing, planning, homelessness, fiscal devolution, public service integration, policing, fire governance and resilience; specific funding and implementation timeline not yet confirmed
findings.quote: The proposals would transfer substantial new responsibilities to Strategic Authorities across skills, employment support, transport, housing, planning, homelessness, fiscal devolution, public service integration, policing, fire governance and resilience

findings.headline: Treasury management income forecast to overachieve by £4.271m, driven by higher cash balances and interest rates
findings.detail: Treasury management income overachievement of £4.271m forecast. Driven by cash balances being higher than anticipated due to capital programme slippage and delays in spend, combined with new funding received in advance of expenditure. Additional overachievement reflects higher interest rates earned on liquidity balances than anticipated in budget.
findings.matters: Positive variance is contingent on capital slippage continuing; shows authority's cash management is benefiting from high interest rate environment but masks underlying capital programme underperformance; creates dependency on continued investment returns.
findings.figures: £4.271m overachievement of Treasury Management Income against budget
findings.quote: £4.271m overachievement of Treasury Management Income against budget. This increase in forecast is driven by a combination the Authority's cash balances being higher than anticipated due to delays in spend on the capital programme set out earlier in the outturn report, and new funding being received in advance of spend.

findings.headline: £1.741m revenue underspend forecast, predominantly due to timing rather than structural savings
findings.detail: Combined Authority forecasts full-year revenue outturn of £78.748m against budget of £80.489m. Underspend spread across Place and Economy (£912k underspend) and Transport (£843k underspend). Specific variances include £551k Active Travel slippage due to recruitment challenges, £300k Health and Wellbeing Strategy reprofiling, £300k Resilience Plan Phase 2 moved to 2027/28, and £250k Growth Hub underspend following transfer of export programme to national delivery.
findings.matters: Paper indicates variances expected to recover in latter quarters through timing catch-up rather than representing permanent savings; demonstrates revenue delivery is dependent on project acceleration and that early-quarter spend lags delivery partner claims profiles.
findings.figures: £1.741m revenue underspend forecast; Place and Economy -£912k, Transport -£843k, Active Travel -£551k, Health and Wellbeing -£300k, Resilience Phase 2 -£300k
findings.quote: the majority of service areas are forecasting to spend to budget

findings.headline: £48.150m of in-year capital budgets require rephasing into future years
findings.detail: Review of project budgets following 2025/26 slippage has identified material movements into future years. Key components include £21.000m for bus depots, £7.413m for Local Growth Fund delivery, £3.500m Skills Capital, and £3.173m Resilience Plan Capital. Majority of rephasing relates to budgets allocated to funds or schemes still requiring business case approval via the Single Assurance Framework, rather than in-delivery projects.
findings.matters: Shows extent of capital programme delays and uncommitted spending; indicates delivery acceleration will be required in latter quarters to meet annual targets and demonstrates reliance on SAF approval process for programme progression.
findings.figures: £48.150m capital rephasing (of £107.397m total capital budget); including £21.000m bus depots, £7.413m Local Growth Fund, £3.500m Skills Capital, £3.173m Resilience Plan Capital, £3.000m A10, £2.500m A141, £2.707m bus network improvements
findings.quote: £48.150m of the in-year capital budgets require rephasing. This includes both approved budgets and those that remain subject to approval.

findings.detail: Residual risk score rose from 12 through December 2025 to 17 by March 2026 and remained at 17 through June 2026. The risk register notes threats are not yet sufficiently understood and mitigated, and opportunities are not maximised.

findings.detail: The residual risk score declined from 14 through March 2026 to 10 by June 2026, suggesting an improved control environment and reduced likelihood of internal fraud.
findings.matters: Internal control quality signals organisational maturity to lenders; improved fraud controls indicate strengthened governance and reduced financial misstatement risk.

findings.paper_title: Closure of Subsidiary Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Business Growth Company Limited
findings.headline: Subsidiary company being formally wound up following solvency statement
findings.detail: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Growth Company Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Combined Authority, is being closed through an approved capital reduction in shareholding. The process relies on a solvency statement dated 13 August 2026 confirming the company can be wound up, following a closure decision made 23 months earlier in October 2024.
findings.matters: A lender needs to know what entities sit within the borrowing group structure and whether subsidiary closures leave any unresolved liabilities or guarantees outstanding.
findings.figures: Decision date: October 2024; Solvency statement: 13.08.2026
findings.quote: In order to finalise the winding up stage and closure of the Combined Authority Growth Co subsidiary, the Committee is asked to recommend to the Combined Authority Board the approval to reduce shareholding in Growth Co in order to complete an orderly winding up of the company.

findings.headline: New data protection risk added to register regarding potential non-compliance with UK GDPR in transfer of personal data outside the EU.
findings.detail: Following engagement with the Data Protection Officer, a new risk has been added to the Corporate Risk Register concerning transfer of personal data outside the EU in ways that could lead to non-compliance with UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018 requirements.
findings.matters: Data protection compliance failures could result in regulatory sanction, fines, and reputational damage, which expose the authority to material governance and financial risk.
findings.figures: 1 new risk added; 17 total risks in register
findings.quote: A new risk has been added to the register following engagement with the Data Protection Officer: 'Transfer of personal data outside the EU leading to non-compliance with UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018 requirements'.

findings.headline: Fraud risk in CPCA downgraded from High to Medium and now within risk appetite following RSM grant funding audit.
findings.detail: The Combined Authority's fraud risk has been reduced following completion of an RSM audit on Grant Funding Agreements. The resulting control actions are being implemented, which has lowered the likelihood score and brought the risk within the organisation's risk appetite.
findings.matters: Improving fraud controls and governance over public funding demonstrates strengthening internal controls, which reduces financial and reputational risk to the authority.
findings.figures: Risk moved from High to Medium; one fewer high risk than previous month
findings.quote: The Fraud Occurring in CPCA risk has reduced from High to Medium and is now within appetite. RSM has completed an audit on Grant Funding Agreements, and the resulting actions are being implemented, reducing the likelihood score.

findings.headline: Failure to prevent fraud offence under Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023 came into force 1 September 2025; Combined Authority in scope
findings.detail: The financial regulations incorporate a new statutory obligation introduced by the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023. The failure to prevent fraud offence came into effect on 1 September 2025, just 12 days before this committee meeting. The Combined Authority must demonstrate that reasonable fraud prevention measures were in place at the time any fraud occurred, or faces criminal liability as an organisation. The regulations specify that reasonable measures include commitment from senior management, fraud risk assessment, proportionate prevention procedures, due diligence, communication and training, and monitoring and review.
findings.matters: A finance director must ensure the organisation has demonstrably adequate fraud prevention measures to avoid criminal liability; a lender would view this as a material new governance obligation affecting organisational risk.
findings.figures: 1 September 2025
findings.quote: The Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023 introduced a number of measures to combat economic crime and improve transparency, including the offence of the failure to prevent fraud which came into force on 1 September 2025. The Combined Authority, which is in scope for the regulations, will need to demonstrate that at the time a fraud was committed there were reasonable fraud prevention measures in place.

findings.headline: Government reviewing Net Zero Hubs programme requirements with announcement expected September 2026; current programme fully government-funded at £12.7m.
findings.detail: The authority's Net Zero Hub programme totals £12.655m for 26/27 and is fully funded from government grant with no call on the authority's own budget. The government is currently reviewing the future requirements for Net Zero Hubs across the country, with an announcement expected around 20 September 2026.
findings.matters: External grant funding subject to government policy review represents a contingency for councils. Lenders and peer finance directors need to understand dependency on government funding and potential for changes in funding or programme requirements.
findings.figures: Current programme £12.655m for 26/27; government announcement expected 20 September 2026
findings.quote: The Government is currently reviewing the future requirements for Net Zero Hubs across the country with an announcement expected around 20 September.

findings.headline: Spatial Development Strategy received additional £1.55m funding to be profiled over delivery period to 2029.
findings.detail: The authority received an additional £1.553846m towards delivery of the Spatial Development Strategy. This funding needs to be profiled over the SDS delivery period to 2029. As a result, the SDS budget is forecast at £0.3m for 26/27 against a budget of £1.983m, creating slippage of £1.683m. The cost of the SDS team and related activity is currently being evaluated.
findings.matters: Lenders and finance directors need to understand changes to funding inflows and how councils manage multi-year spending commitments from grants, which affects financial flexibility and debt capacity.
findings.figures: Additional funding £1.553846m; 26/27 budget £1.983m; forecast £0.3m; slippage £1.683m; profiled to 2029

findings.headline: Health and Wellbeing Strategy activities deferred to future year with £300k forecast underspend against £486k annual budget
findings.detail: Skills revenue expenditure is £165k below budget to date. The full-year revenue forecast is £300k below budget, specifically due to Health and Wellbeing Strategy activities being deferred to the following financial year. This £300k underspend is recorded as a deferral.
findings.matters: Activity deferrals affect multi-year budget planning and may indicate delivery timing challenges extending beyond the current year.
findings.figures: £300k forecast underspend, £300k deferral, £486k original Health and Wellbeing Strategy budget
findings.quote: The forecast is expected to be £300k below budget as the activities required to deliver the Health and Wellbeing Strategy will carry on in the future year.

findings.headline: FE Cold Spots capital programme records zero expenditure to June 2026 despite £4m annual budget and history of delivery challenges
findings.detail: The FE Cold Spots programme is the sole skills capital scheme currently being delivered with a £4m annual budget. No capital expenditure is recorded to the end of June 2026. The report states the programme has 'faced multiple challenges during the years which has affected the timing of its delivery' but expects 'all the funds will be utilised by the end of the current financial year', requiring substantial spending acceleration in the remaining eight months.
findings.matters: Capital programme execution is a material indicator of council capacity to manage large schemes; prior delays make near-year catch-up a material risk.
findings.figures: £4m annual budget, £0 YTD expenditure, 8 months remaining
findings.quote: The programme has faced multiple challenges during the years which has affected the timing of its delivery.

findings.headline: Skills Division grant income £237k above forecast due to approved FE Industry Placement and FE Teacher Industry Exchange programmes
findings.detail: The Combined Authority received £16.1m in skills grant income to June 2026, representing 60% of the £26.9m annual budget. The full-year income forecast is £237k higher than the original budget following approval of FE Industry Placement (£407k) and FE Teacher Industry Exchange (£162k) through the Single Assurance Framework process with funding from DWP.
findings.matters: Grant funding variations affect service delivery capacity and signalling of funding authority priorities; material for multi-year financial planning.
findings.figures: £237k forecast surplus, £407k FE Industry Placement, £162k FE Teacher Industry Exchange, £16.1m YTD income (60% of budget)
findings.quote: The forecast is £237k higher than budget due to ASF additional funds.

findings.headline: Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (LEVI) project £2.5m deferred to future financial years; procurement exercise in progress with work not expected to start until quarter 4.
findings.detail: LEVI was budgeted at £3m for 2026/27 but is now forecast at only £500k, with £2.5m deferred to future years. The paper reports that the project will not commence until Q4 because a procurement exercise is currently in progress. This represents a significant reprofiling of capital delivery in this priority infrastructure area.
findings.matters: Capital project deferrals affect borrowing requirements, cash flow forecasting, and the ability to deliver strategic objectives. A £2.5m deferral driven by procurement delays could signal broader market or specification challenges.
findings.figures: LEVI budget £3,000k; forecast outturn £500k; deferral £2,500k to future years
findings.quote: spend on electric vehicles is expected to slip into future years as the project is now not expected to get underway until quarter 4 of this financial year. A procurement exercise is currently in progress.

findings.headline: CIPFA Bulletin 22 requires implementation of quinquennial revaluation or five-year rolling programme for property valuations from 2025/26.
findings.detail: From 2025/26, Authority must apply CIPFA Bulletin 22 which mandates quinquennial (five-year) revaluation or five-year rolling valuation programme for non-investment property assets, supported by annual indexation in intervening years. This represents change from prior annual revaluation requirement and requires careful management of valuation methodology.
findings.matters: Significant change to valuation methodology and frequency affects timing and basis of property asset valuations; requires careful selection of appropriate indices for years not subject to formal revaluation.
findings.figures: Five-year revaluation cycle requirement
findings.quote: The guidance mandates a quinquennial revaluation or a five-year rolling programme for formal valuations, supported by annual indexation in the intervening years.

findings.headline: Authority holds £46.4 million in long-term investments including £11.1 million in loans to subsidiary companies requiring impairment and recovery testing.
findings.detail: Balance sheet includes £46.4 million in long-term investments of which £11.1 million represents loans issued to subsidiary companies repayable over varying periods. Auditor will test assumptions and sensitivities used in impairment calculations and assess management's recoverability assessment against group performance.
findings.matters: Significant investment in subsidiaries, particularly loans, requires assurance over recovery risk and balance sheet valuation; material element of group financial position and potential exposure if subsidiaries underperform.
findings.figures: £46.4 million total long-term investments; £11.1 million subsidiary loans; investment balance £0.046 billion
findings.quote: As at 31 March 2025 the Authority holds Long-Term Investments of £46.4 million in the Balance Sheet, of which £11.1 million relates to loans issued to subsidiary companies.

findings.headline: Building held by subsidiary reclassified from investment property to operational asset with upward valuation of £11.996 million in 2024/25.
findings.detail: University building held by Peterborough R&D Property Company was reclassified in group accounts from Investment Property at Fair Value to Property, Plant and Equipment at Depreciated Replacement Cost in 2024/25. The reclassification resulted in upward valuation of £11.996 million and recognition of accumulated depreciation of £0.542 million from 2021/22.
findings.matters: Step-change in valuation of material group asset affects group balance sheet position and indicates prior accounting treatment may not have captured true economic position; significant revaluation movements suggest asset base may have been understated.
findings.figures: Upward revaluation £11.996 million; accumulated depreciation £0.542 million from 2021/22
findings.quote: This reclassification has resulted in an upward valuation of £11.996 million and the recognition of accumulated depreciation of £0.542 million from 2021/22.

findings.headline: Three internal control recommendations from 2024/25 audit remain outstanding: journal authorisation, contract documentation, and loan agreements.
findings.detail: Auditor identified three control weaknesses in 2024/25 that remain unresolved: no formal procedure for authorising manual journals before posting to general ledger; contract variations not retained to support audit trail; loan facility agreements found undated and unsigned. All three will be followed up in 2025/26 audit.
findings.matters: Unresolved control deficiencies in journal authorisation, contracts, and loan agreements indicate gaps in financial oversight that increase risk of error or fraud in financial statements.
findings.figures: Three recommendations outstanding from prior audit
findings.quote: The Authority does not have any formal procedure for the authorisation of manual journals before they are posted to the General Ledger. This represents a level of weakness in the Authority's overall control environment and increases the potential risk of Management Override

findings.headline: Auditor expects limited assurance over opening balances at 1 April 2025 and closing reserves balance at 31 March 2026 due to continuing gaps in assurance.
findings.detail: Auditor anticipates limited assurance over opening balances and closing reserves for 2025/26 due to continuing lack of evidence over Pension Scheme Liability/Asset and Other Long-Term Liabilities. This is driving requirement for historic rebuild work on 2022/23 and earlier years. Key uncertainties remain unresolved from prior periods.
findings.matters: Reserve balances are critical to understanding a council's financial sustainability and ability to manage unexpected shocks; gaps in assurance prevent clear view of true financial position.
findings.figures: Year ended 31 March 2025; positions as at 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026
findings.quote: As a result, we anticipate that for 2025/26: We will have limited assurance over the opening balances for 2025/26; and Limited assurance over the closing reserves balance, due to uncertainty over the opening amount.

findings.headline: Authority issued disclaimer opinions on financial statements for both 2023/24 and 2024/25 and expects limited assurance for 2025/26.
findings.detail: Auditor was unable to form an opinion on the Authority's financial statements in 2023/24 and 2024/25 due to application of the audit backstop, indicating material gaps in financial reporting arrangements. The Authority is following NAO recovery guidance with expected progression from disclaimer to qualified to eventually unqualified opinion over multiple years. For 2025/26, auditor anticipates limited assurance, continuing the multi-year rebuild process.
findings.matters: Finance directors and lenders need assurance that a council's accounts are reliable; two consecutive disclaimer opinions indicate significant gaps in financial reporting and control environment.
findings.quote: In the audit reports for the years ended 31 March 2024 and 31 March 2025, a disclaimer of opinion was issued due to the application of the backstop. This means the auditor has not been able to form an opinion on the financial statements.

findings.headline: Integrated Settlement readiness assessment completed with gap analysis and work programme scoped
findings.detail: The Combined Authority completed an internal self-assessment and evidence-gathering exercise during 2025/26 against Integrated Settlement readiness criteria from MHCLG covering four capability areas (strategic planning, people and capability, financial and performance management, and reporting and evaluation). A gap analysis has been completed and a work programme to address identified gaps is being scoped for delivery.
findings.matters: Integrated Settlements are expected to bring additional devolved powers and funding to councils demonstrating readiness. Early preparation positions a council to access future funding and shows governance maturity.
findings.figures: Four capability areas assessed at four levels each; Core level considered ready for settlement
findings.quote: Following the initial self-assessment against the Integrated Settlement readiness criteria provided by MHCLG, the Combined Authority has completed a gap analysis and a work programme to address the gaps identified is being scoped and will be delivered to ensure that we can demonstrate that we achieve the required level of control maturity to support a future Integrated Settlement

findings.headline: Best Value Notice concluded following independent oversight completion
findings.detail: The Combined Authority's second Best Value Notice concluded in September 2024. The Independent Advisory and Support Group providing oversight concluded their support in June 2025. The Authority reports this signals recovery and that Best Value commitment is now embedded in regular governance processes.
findings.matters: Exit from Best Value Notice indicates a council has recovered from a period of governance or financial stress and returned to standard compliance status.
findings.figures: Second Best Value Notice concluded September 2024; oversight concluded June 2025
findings.quote: Following the conclusion of the second Best Value Notice in September 2024 the Combined Authority's Independent Advisory and Support Group concluded their support in June 2025, following the Mayoral election.
